revisions.body: The opening first corrects the listener’s position. Glaucon treats the banquet as recent enough for Apollodorus to have been there; Apollodorus answers by placing it in his childhood and naming Aristodemus as the attendee from whom he heard it. The listener must therefore separate presence, recollection, and verification before receiving the speeches. I read that calibration as the frame’s first intellectual demand.

Eryximachus makes the new activity a distributed form: each person is to speak in turn, praise Eros as beautifully as possible, and let Phaedrus begin. The point is not merely that speeches replace music; the table itself becomes the instrument of the event, assigning every guest a turn and a common object. I read this arrangement as a shift from passive entertainment to shared authorship: the feast will now be made by the speeches it solicits.

Diotima uses Alcestis, Achilles, and Codrus to press a larger thesis: human beings will risk everything for the immortal memory of virtue and renown. The examples therefore do not stand only as heroic deaths to admire; within her argument, they become evidence for love’s orientation toward immortality. I hear this as a reframing of courage: the question is no longer merely whether the deed is noble, but what kind of immortality the deed is meant to secure.
